correctness.rationale: The real Hilbert–Schmidt dissipation vanishes on an eigenmatrix with imaginary eigenvalue only if its off-diagonals and trap row/column vanish; the star-edge commutator then forces every diagonal entry to equal the zero trap entry. Thus for positive rates the resolvent gives the unconditional survival integral. Averaging the leaf-localized input over nontrap leaves preserves survival. With m=N−2, integrating the center and nontrap populations gives A=1/(2J), B=−1/(2Jm), and trace flux gives Q=1/κ. The real leaf-pair equations give C=(m−1)/(m(2γ+κ)) and, when m>1, D=−1/(mγ). The two center–leaf coherence equations then eliminate P and O; P+Q+mO gives the five coefficients as stated. The separate reciprocal terms yield strict convexity and together with the positive linear terms give compact sublevel sets for N≥4. The fixed-κ stationarity equation decreases strictly in γ and its right side decreases strictly as κ increases; the two limiting equations yield the stated strict bounds. At N=3 there is only one ordinary leaf: even at γ=0 a zero-dissipation eigenmatrix must have trap row/column zero; their eigen-equations force the center row/column zero, and the center–ordinary-leaf equations then force the remaining entry zero. The boundary formula is consequently a finite mean and has minimum √6/J at κ=√6J. If one insists on γ>0 also at N=3, this is an infimum only, as distinguished by the stated boundary case. For the large-star claim, comparison with any positive test pair on s=2 and positivity of the exact five terms first bound s=2a+b above and away from zero. The displayed scaled decomposition then bounds 1/b+(1−3/N)/a, since its negative terms are bounded and the leading term is at least N after dividing by √N. Interior limits minimize the subleading coefficient on s=2. Its strict convexity and equation a^4−2a^3+4a−2=0 give the stated root (put z=2a−1 and factor the equation as (z²+3)²−12(z−1)²=0). The b-stationarity equation gives N(1/4−1/s²)=O(1); thus the residual leading cost N(s−2)²/(4s) vanishes in the rescaled second term, giving c=f(a_*).
residual_risks: The independent matrix examples are finite numerical checks only. The boundary minimum uses γ=0; the interior theorem uses positive rates and starts at N=4. No claim is made about other initial states or trap locations.

value.rationale: Moving the sink to a leaf creates a genuinely coupled control problem: the optimal growth exponent differs from hub capture, and a flat leading order leaves the separate rates undetermined until the second term. The exact formula, sharp two-term optimization and persistence of an interior optimum for N≥4 answer this natural comparison rather than merely changing rate notation.
residual_risks: Value concerns the specified Markovian model and a single localized initial excitation. The review makes no experimental or device-performance claim.
